samples.summary: New Esc/arrow guard only recognises Radix-style overlays (`data-state="open"` + role, or a popper-wrapper child); the repo also has hand-rolled `role="dialog"` popovers with no `data-state`, which would bypass it
samples.evidence: Out-of-diff overlays that close themselves on Escape but carry no `data-state`: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/components/comments/CommentPopover.tsx:83, packages/frontend/src/app/docs/comments/DocsCommentPopover.tsx:80, packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:618. None of them matches OPEN_OVERLAY_SELECTOR, so if any such popover is ever mounted on the `/f/:id` image route the Esc that dismisses it would also fire `onClose` and navigate the user off the viewer — exactly the failure mode the guard was added to prevent. I could not prove any of these three is reachable on the image route today (they live on the sheets/docs editor routes), so the defect is latent rather than live. Note also that the repo already has an overlay-detection convention the new selector diverges from: packages/frontend/src/app/slides/slides-image-input.ts:171 uses `[role="dialog"], [role="alertdialog"], [aria-modal="true"]`. To confirm: check whether any non-Radix overlay (comment popover, custom lightbox, `aria-modal` panel) can render inside FileShell for an image document.
searchedFor: read components/ui/dialog.tsx, ui/sheet.tsx, share-dialog.tsx for Radix role/data-state

samples.summary: Second ImageViewer consumer (anonymous share route) inherits the bubble→capture listener change and the new DOM-querying guard without being considered in the diff
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:766 renders `<ImageViewer documentId={resolved.documentId} token={token} />`. After this change that mount registers its window `keydown` listener in the CAPTURE phase (image-viewer.tsx:163) and runs `document.querySelector(OPEN_OVERLAY_SELECTOR)` on every keystroke of the share page. Because `onClose` is omitted and both sibling queries are `enabled: !token`, the handler is effectively inert there, so I found no user-visible breakage — but the phase change means no component on the share page can suppress the viewer's key handling via `stopPropagation` any more, which is a contract change for that consumer that the diff never touches.

samples.summary: The two other FileShell consumers (PDF and generic-file layouts) pass no `headerLeading`, so the new back affordance exists only for images
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/files/file-detail.tsx:94 (PdfFileLayout) and :171 (GenericFileLayout) mount FileShell with `headerActions` only, leaving `/f/:id` inconsistent across document types. This is an explicit non-goal — docs/tasks/active/20260822-image-viewer-back-button-todo.md:44-46 records it — so it is recorded for completeness only, not as a defect.

verdict.reason: The three cited hand-rolled `role="dialog"` overlays do exist and do lack `data-state`, so they genuinely would not match OPEN_OVERLAY_SELECTOR — but none of them can be mounted on any route where the guard runs, so there is no reachable bypass. ImageViewer has exactly two mount sites: file-detail.tsx:152 (via ImageFileLayout, only for `type === "image"`) and shared-document.tsx:766, and the latter passes no `onClose` at all, making Esc inert (image-viewer.tsx:161). ImageFileLayout (file-detail.tsx:136-154) renders only FileShell + BackToDocumentsButton + DownloadFileButton + ShareDialog + ImageViewer, and FileShell (file-shell.tsx:108-131) adds only SidebarProvider/AppSidebar/SiteHeader — every overlay in that subtree is Radix and carries `data-state`. The cited popovers are rendered exclusively from docs-view.tsx:599/618 and sheet-view.tsx:1670, sibling route trees that never co-mount with the `/f/:id` FileDetail route; no shared component in the image subtree renders them. A repo-wide grep for `role="dialog|alertdialog|menu|listbox"|aria-modal` surfaces no other non-Radix overlay in the image route's tree. The only Escape handler actually co-mounted on the image route, site-header.tsx:66 (title-rename input), is already excluded by the INPUT/TEXTAREA/contentEditable early return at image-viewer.tsx:149-156. The divergence from the slides-image-input.ts:171 selector convention is a consistency observation, not a reachable bypass, and the finding itself concedes the defect is latent rather than live.
